title: Model docking and version anchoring pipeline for community LLM weights
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Goal: Build an end-to-end automated pipeline to take new community/open LLM weight bundles from raw artifact arrival through format conversion, deterministic validation, version anchoring (pinning), and publishing of a lightweight performance profile. The pipeline must be robust to heterogeneous checkpoints (sharded, safetensors/hf, custom bundled formats), provide deterministic smoke validation, surface license/compliance flags, and emit artifacts that the serving runtime and Console can consume (canonical version id, quantized candidate pointers, published perf metrics).

Scope includes:
- Ingest worker that downloads manifests and runs provenance checks (signatures, checksums, license detection).
- Containerized conversion service with pluggable backends (transformers, custom scripts) and deterministic output hashing to enable reproducible pins.
- Validation harness: end-to-end forward-pass smoke tests (float & int8 candidates), memory/latency profiling on representative infra, and correctness checks against golden prompts.
- Anchoring step: choose canonical version id (semantic plus content-hash), create a stable pin record, and publish to model-catalog with metadata required for serving (architecture, tokenizer fingerprint, kv-cache shape hints).
- Profile publish: generate and persist a compact performance profile (P50/P95 tokens/sec, typical latency for 32/256 token lengths, recommended batch/kvcache settings, quantization compatibility notes).
- Integration: emit telemetry and traces to Console dashboards and surface canary run results for a staged rollout.

Non-goals: onboarding proprietary customer weights; full safety evals and moderation (these are separate flows).

Acceptance criteria:
- New community weight bundle can flow from S3 arrival to a pinned catalog entry with profile within 24 hours (typical case).
- Deterministic conversion: identical input -> identical canonical artifact hash across runs.
- Smoke validation runs on x86 CPU and a single A100 instance, producing latency and memory metrics.
- Catalog entry consumed by serving infra to create a staging canary without manual intervention.

Operational concerns: license flags requiring legal/OSS team gating; potential heavy resource usage during conversion (need quotas); edge cases with massive sharded checkpoints (>120GB) must fallback to staged conversion with streaming transforms.
